 Singapore’s beverage container return scheme has been battered with criticisms. Why do we need it?
 Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox
 The scheme could help to improve Singapore’s low domestic recycling rates.
 Audrey Tan
 Published   Nov 03, 2026, 10:00 AM
 Updated   Nov 03, 2026, 10:00 AM
 Set as preferred source Listen 中文 The scheme could help to improve Singapore’s low domestic recycling rates.
 Blue recycling bins filled with non-recyclable trash have become a common sight around Singapore. This contamination has resulted in poor domestic recycling rates in the country, as food and liquid waste thrown into the commingled bins taints the other recyclables. 
 To overcome this challenge, the National Environment Agency on Oct 1 fully implemented its Beverage Container Return Scheme (BCRS) to ensure that plastic bottles and cans are segregated for recycling. But this initiative has also been plagued with complaints. 
 In this episode, host Audrey Tan chats with Ang Qing and Shabana Begum, environment correspondents at ST, on whether these criticisms are warranted, and whether Singapore should continue pushing ahead with the scheme.
